content.title: About
content.content: Moo Goo Gai Pan is a classic Chinese dish made with chicken breast, shiitake mushrooms, and vegetables, cooked in a light soy‑ginger‑garlic sauce. It has a delicate, mildly salty and slightly sweet flavor and is often served over rice.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name “Moo Goo Gai Pan” means “chicken with mushrooms” in Cantonese.
The dish originated in Canton in the early 20th century and quickly spread to Chinese restaurants worldwide.
Traditionally it uses skinless chicken breast, making it a relatively low‑fat option.
Shiitake mushrooms add a strong umami taste and are rich in B‑vitamins.
Original recipes sometimes include toasted cashews or almonds for added crunch.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken breast provides a high‑quality source of protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Skinless chicken and minimal oil keep the dish low in total fat, suitable for lean‑diet plans.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Shiitake mushrooms contain niacin, riboflavin, and vitamin B6, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Shiitake mushrooms are rich in polysaccharides (lentinan) and ergothioneine, which have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Beta‑glucans in mushrooms may help strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Allergy to chicken or mushrooms
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken meat or shiitake mushrooms.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce adds a notable amount of salt; those monitoring sodium should use low‑sodium soy sauce.

items.title: MSG presence
items.content: The dish may contain monosodium glutamate, which can cause headaches or flushing in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Serve
content.content: Moo Goo Gai Pan is served hot, typically alongside steamed rice or noodles. Garnish with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds. For extra heat, add a dash of chili sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2–3 days. Reheat in a skillet or microwave, adding a splash of water to retain moisture.
